detail.title: Identity as a Predictive Self-Model
detail.summary: This journal entry initiates inquiry into identity within the enforced research topic. We theorize identity not as a static entity, but as a dynamic predictive construct that sustains continuity despite shifting cognitive and physiological states. By framing the self as a model maintained through active inference, we aim to address how continuity of experience emerges from transient data points. Future research will explore the alignment between this predictive self-model and memory-based persistence.

detail.statement: Identity is a persistent self-model maintained by predictive processing, where continuity arises from the iterative minimization of prediction error between expected and observed state transitions.
detail.reason: Existing evidence on active inference and curiosity-driven exploration suggests that systems maintain stability by predicting future states; this mechanism is plausibly extended to the construction of a self-model.
